name: Blow dryer + round brush

lead: A blow dryer pushes heated air through hair while a round brush adds tension and curve, which lifts the roots and sets volume. The combination is used to create a fuller, shaped result than air-drying provides.
It is widely recommended for thinning hair and fine hair, where lift at the crown and hairline makes the hair look denser. Technique, rather than equipment price, has the biggest effect.

paras: Heat evaporates water and temporarily breaks hydrogen bonds in the hair keratin. Hair cooled in a lifted or curved shape re-forms those bonds, holding the style until moisture returns.

Heat damage is the main caveat. Studies on tresses show lifted and cracked cuticles with high temperatures, and the damage grows with heat and with drying very wet hair. Holding the dryer at a distance, keeping it moving, towel-drying first and using heat protectants reduce harm, and some reviews note air-drying is not clearly safer. Results are short-term and reset with each wash.
